To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

photodetachment of isolated model anion chromphores of green fluorescent protein (GFP) and cyan fluorescent protein (CFP) has been measured, with a vertical detachment energy of 2.9 eV to the ground state of the radical and a second, higher energy, detachment to the first excited state of the radical.
the photodetachment energy of the green and blue fluorescent protein chromophores are 2.85 and 2.88 eV, respectively.

the vertical photodetection energies of the model green and cyan fluorescent protein chromphore anions were determined and that the photodetachment process is complicated by the autoionization of excited electronic states of chromophore anionic species.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the photophysics of the chromophores that make the green and cyan variants of the fluorescent proteins so useful in biology.
the photophysical and electronic properties of protein chromophore radicals, a class of species which has not been studied previously.

the photophysics of the chromophores of two of the most important fluorescent proteins, and the photodetachment spectroscopy of the deprotonated chromophores provides new insights into the photophysics and the electronic structures of these chromophores.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the photodetachment energy from the ground electronic states of the isolated protein anion chromophore to the ground electronic state is similar to 3 eV.

photodetachment of the protein chromophore model anion is a two-step process, involving first the detachment of an electron from the ground state of the anions, and then the detachment of an additional electron from the excited state of the anionic chromophore.
the anion chromophore of the green fluorescent protein is more easily reduced than that of the cyan fluorescent protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the isolated model chromophore anionic chromophores of green and cyan fluorescent protein can be used as electron donors in biological systems.
the isolated model chromophore anionic chromophores of both the green and cyan variants of the GFPs are good electron donors.
the photodetachment of the isolated protein anion chromophore is not a viable electron transfer mechanism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
photodetachment of isolated protein chromophores anions is a viable route to generate protein chromophore radicals.

the vertical photodetection energies of isolated model chromophore anionic species of the green and the cyan fluorescent proteins are significantly lower than the vertical ionization energies of the corresponding neutral chromophores.
, in the case of the green fluorescent protein chromphore, detachment to the excited electronic state of the neutral radical is energetically more favorable than to the ground electronic state.
